newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HORSE RACING-HK JOCKEY CLUB SUSPENDS SEVEN TRAINERS, JOCKEYS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-HK JOCKEY CLUB SUSPENDS SEVEN TRAINERS, JOCKEYS.

text.p: The Hong Kong Jockey Club said on Tuesday it had suspended the licences of two trainers, two jockeys and three apprentice jockeys.
The suspensions follow a major race fixing and illegal betting scandal in the British colony in which 37 people have been hauled in for questioning in the past two days.
The two trainers were Chan Pak-Hung and Leung Sik-Lun. The two jockeys were Yim Hin-Keung and Choi Chun-Wai. The three apprentice jockeys were Ho Wah-Lun, Tam Shu-Man and Ko Chun-Ho.
Licences of all five would be suspended until April 2, or until a time determined by stewards of the club, the Jockey Club said in a statement.
The suspensions were "to maintain the confidence of the public in the conduct of racing", the statement said.
Hong Kong graft busters have already charged five other people with taking illegal bets and the Jockey Club has vowed a clean-up campaign after one of the territory's worst horse racing scandals.
